col.cost95: Cost in a bad year, P95 (€)
help.priority: Each row is a catchment. Phosphorus and nitrogen show how much of these nutrients Apetit's contract fields deliver to that water each year. The priority score combines that load with the water's ecological status and sensitivity: higher means act there first.
help.hotspots: The individual fields that lose the most phosphorus to water, with the most likely cause turned into a concrete action for the farming advisor.
help.materiality: Purchased raw materials ranked by how much nature risk they carry: their emissions, the pressures their production puts on nature, and the state of nature in the origin country.
help.risk: How much the average yield of each contract crop is expected to change in 2041–2060 compared with 1991–2020, and how often a bad year (yield below 80 % of normal) would occur. Negative = lower yields.
help.eur: What poor harvests would cost Apetit: the shortfall must be bought as imports at the contract price plus an import premium. P95 is the cost in a 1-in-20 bad year.
help.backtest: Validation: the model was trained on data up to 2019 and tested on 2020–2026. It is compared with a simple baseline (each farm's historical average). Smaller error is better.
help.lines: Each line item is a group of emissions, e.g. one fuel at one plant or one raw material from one supplier. Click one to see the source records behind it.
help.lineage: Emissions = activity amount × emission factor, for each source record. Corrections show where the raw data was changed and whether a reviewer approved it.
help.peat: Contract-farm emissions per crop: Juuri's estimate (including drained peat soils) next to today's calculator, which assumes mineral soil everywhere.
help.base_years: Possible base years for the climate targets. The 2025 base adjusted for the Foodhills acquisition is recommended.
help.levers: Actions that reduce emissions: how many tonnes each saves per year at full effect, what it costs per tonne (negative = saves money), and who would own it.
help.macc: The bar shows how far the actions take us towards the target. Each block is one action; its length is the emissions it cuts per year. Actions are added cheapest first. The red line is where the target is reached.
help.drought: For each crop: the season-to-date effect of the weather streamed from the stations on expected yield, and how many parcels have a drought alert.
chart.hint: Drag to zoom · double-click or ⌂ in the toolbar to reset · 📷 to download
macc.summary: To close the {boundary} gap of {gap} by {year}, the cheapest route is: {list}. Together they avoid {t} per year at a net cost of {cost} per year.
macc.short: All selected {boundary} levers together avoid {t} per year — still {short} short of the {year} target. More levers or deeper changes are needed.
macc.no_gap: {boundary} is already on track for {year} without additional levers.
macc.step_save: cuts {t} a year and saves {eur} a year
macc.step_cost: cuts {t} a year and costs {eur} a year ({pt} per tonne)
